crossRefs.note: “ ‘Why, then, have you brought me out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no eye had seen me.
I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
For Yahweh had closed up tight all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
but to Hannah he gave a double portion, for he loved Hannah, but Yahweh had shut up her womb.
If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not…
because he didn’t kill me from the womb. So my mother would have been my grave, and her womb always great.
“Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
“My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
“Even today my complaint is rebellious. His hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, and put away evil from your flesh; for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.

translations.web: because it didn’t shut up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.
translations.bsb: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
translations.kjv: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother's womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.
translations.asv: Because it shut not up the doors of my mothers' womb, Nor hid trouble from mine eyes.
